source_text.diagnosis: Q-1037 / GH #2364: print per-partition and host diagnostics when the watchdog fires.

result.summary: REVIEWER PASS, no MAJOR. Diag call sits after the unchanged WARNING echo and before kill -TERM; WARNING text, TERM/KILL, exit codes and EXIT trap untouched; nothing printed on a normal run (only reached inside the kill -0 branch). Output goes to stderr like the WARNING. Script has set -u and set -m only (no set -e, no pipefail), so the pipelines cannot abort anything; the call is also guarded with || true. part_start_epoch is declared before the fork so the subshell sees a copy, and ${part_start_epoch[$idx]:-$now} is set -u safe (verified with an unset index). The function is defined before the watchdog fork. mkdir lock verified: 4 concurrent invocations produced exactly one DIAG host block. timeout wraps only binaries (uptime, cat, free, df, nproc); no shell function is passed to timeout. ps fallback: `( ps --sort ... 2>/dev/null || ps 2>&1 ) | head -9` does fall back when --sort is unsupported (verified on Cygwin ps) and head bounds the output. sed prefix: $pfx contains only the integer partition index and constant text, and the log path is echoed outside sed, so no / or & can break the s/// (log content as sed input verified fine with a/b&c). tail -n 40 and one grep pass are bounded. MINOR items below.

issues.description: ps is not wrapped in timeout 5 (only the test_parallel_diag_run binaries are); a ps hung on a wedged /proc would block this watchdog before kill -TERM and the partition would never be signalled. Wrap it: `timeout 5 ps ... || timeout 5 ps` when timeout exists.

Worst-case delay before TERM is about 5 s x 5 timeout-wrapped commands plus the unbounded ps (about 25 s+); acceptable against the 1800 s timeout and only on a slow host, but a single outer timeout around the host block would cap it.
grep for tests-finished reads the whole log (not tail-limited); fine for normal logs, unbounded for a pathological multi-GB log. Not timeout-wrapped. The 'approx' label covers accuracy, not time.
On a Windows host timeout may resolve to timeout.exe (only /usr/bin/timeout seen in Git Bash here); CI is Linux so not an issue there.
